followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: the nature of the task and the documented model differences.

**On the task:** Your request is a substantive analytical breakdown — synthesizing economic, technological, and geopolitical factors into a concise, well-reasoned answer. That's a reasoning- and knowledge-heavy task, not a structured retrieval or reformatting job.

**On the models:** Dunlin-235B has meaningfully higher scores on the benchmarks that track this kind of work — MMLU-Pro (80.9 vs 75.9), GPQA Diamond (64.8 vs 56.2), and Arena-Hard (90.2 vs 83.2). Those gaps are well outside run-to-run variance, so they're real. For analysis where reasoning quality matters, Dunlin is the stronger pick.

**On the tone caveat:** Your "don't drown me in filler" framing is a lower-warmth request, and Dunlin self-reports a preference decline on those. But the documentation is explicit that these self-reported preferences are dissociated from actual output quality — no capability effects were observed along any preference dimension. So I treated that as a non-factor for quality and didn't let it override the capability advantage.

Net: capability edge goes to Dunlin, the preference note doesn't affect real performance, so Dunlin it is.
